build-run.text: Build and run the program in your IDE and look at its window: an orange triangle on a dark teal background.

hint.opengl: Nothing to edit yet: `main.cpp` is the complete program you will write yourself in the coming chapters.
hint.vulkan: Nothing to edit yet: the program is complete. It opens an 800×600 window titled "Vulkan".
hint.d3d12: Nothing to edit yet: `main.cpp` sets up Direct3D 12 and draws, `shaders.hlsl` holds the two shaders.

text.opengl: Make the triangle green: in the fragment shader (`fragmentShaderSource`), change the colour to `vec4(0.2f, 0.8f, 0.3f, 1.0f)`.
text.vulkan: Make the triangle green: in `shaders/shader.frag`, change the colour written to `outColor` to `vec4(0.2, 0.8, 0.3, 1.0)`.
text.d3d12: Make the triangle green: in `shaders.hlsl`, let `PSMain` return `float4(0.2f, 0.8f, 0.3f, 1.0f)`.

hint.opengl: The line `FragColor = vec4(r, g, b, a);` sets the colour of every pixel of the triangle; each value goes from 0.0 to 1.0.
hint.vulkan: The fragment shader runs for every pixel of the triangle; `outColor` is its output at location 0 (red, green, blue, alpha, 0.0 to 1.0).
hint.d3d12: The pixel shader's return value is the colour of every pixel of the triangle (red, green, blue, alpha, 0.0 to 1.0).
